**Global Consumer Brand – Geo‑Political Activism Response & Communication Playbook (Version 2027‑01‑15)** --- ## 1. Purpose & Vision - **Mission:** Preserve brand integrity, trust, and commercial performance in the face of region‑specific geopolitical consumer activism. - **Guiding Principle:** *Unified, values‑driven messaging that respects local context and never endorses any political stance that could trigger legal or reputational risk.* --- ## 2. Consolidated Governance Architecture | Role | Authority | Decision Triggers | Timing & Escalation | Key Outputs | |------|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|-------------| | **Global Strategic Steering Committee (SSC)** | Final approval of any public global stance (GPS) *or* statement of “No Global Position.” | • Political event affecting ≥ 2 markets
• Consumer sentiment spike > 10 %
• Legal risk flagged | • **24 h** maximum lag from trigger to decision.
• If > 24 h: Flag for Board emergency call; proceed with “Wait‑for‑SSC” path. | - GPS memo (PDF, 5 pages)
- Risk register addendum | | **Regional Response Team (RRT)** | Draft region‑specific narrative, adjust messaging within global framework, submit “Local Adaptation Package.” | • SSC decision
• Local regulatory alert | • **12 h** from SSC decision to draft.
• If > 12 h: Immediate escalation to SSC (auto‑flag). | - Region‑Adaptation Document (Word, 3 pages)
- Local compliance checklist | | **Crisis Communication Lead (CCL)** | Execute release, monitor real‑time sentiment, coordinate cross‑channel updates. | • RRT package ready, SSC statement confirmed.
• Real‑time metrics breach thresholds. | • **1 h** from RRT lock‑in to first publish. | - Real‑time dashboard (dashboards.x) | | **Legal & Compliance Advisor (LCA)** | Validate all public content against local laws. | • Any public statement drafted. | • **< 2 h** turnaround on check. | - Legal clearance memo (PDF) | | **Employee Advocacy & Support (EAS)** | Internal communication, Q&A, morale support. | • External crisis event or release. | • **24 h** first internal memo; **weekly** ongoing cadence. | - Internal memos (PDF/HTML) | | **Franchisee Support Team (FST)** | Provide franchise‑specific kits, training, and FAQ updates. | • External crisis event or external statement. | • **24 h** initial kit; **bi‑weekly pulse calls** thereafter. | - Franchisee Pulse Call deck (PowerPoint) | | **Supply‑Chain & NGO Liaison (SC‑NGL)** | Manage supplier and NGO stakeholder engagement. | • Crisis event affecting supply chain or community perception. | • **48 h** to flag suppliers or NGOs. | - Supplier/NGO contact list (Excel) | *Escalation Flow:* Trigger → **Legal Review** → **SSC** → **RRT** → **CCL** → *Execute* → **Monitoring**. All documents are version‑controlled in the shared “Crisis Playbook” Google Drive folder. The top‑level folder contains a single “Current GPS” file that is amended only after SSC sign‑off. --- ## 3. Dual‑Story Management & Reconciliation ### 3.1 Unified “Principle Statement” All region‑specific adaptations must reference this 73‑word “Principle Statement” that captures the global values. It is mandatory in every press release, social media post, and internal memo. > **Principle Statement** > *“We honour the diverse voices of our communities; we are committed to safe, respectful, and transparent commerce for all. Throughout every market we balance our global values and local realities, never endorsing any political agenda.”* ### 3.2 Reconciliation Process 1. **Draft Review:** RRT files adaptations to the SOC (Shared Operations Center) portal. 2. **Automated Consistency Check:** A lightweight lint tool (`consistency-checker.py`) scans for deviations > 18 characters from the Principle Statement or violates the tone‑rubric (see §5). 3. **Flag & Fix:** Any flag automatically sends a ticket to RRT. 4. **Approval:** After compliance clearance, a single global release is published; regional versions are posted within 30 seconds. A dashboard (Power BI) visualises all adaptations in real time, with color‑coding (green=consistent, yellow=borderline, red=issue). --- ## 4. Expanded Stakeholder Mapping | Stakeholder | Primary Concern | Engagement Frequency | Impact Metric | Weight | |-------------|-----------------|-----------------------|---------------|--------| | **Consumers** | Product integrity, transparency | Real‑time sentiment monitoring | SOV | 30% | | **Franchisees** | Revenue, brand reputation | Franchisee Pulse Calls & portal | Franchise Satisfaction Score | 20% | | **Employees** | Job security, brand values | Weekly Town‑Hall + email | Employee Net‑Promoter Score | 15% | | **Suppliers** | Contract stability, payment terms | Supplier Safety Net Review | On‑time Delivery % | 10% | | **NGOs** | Community impact, sustainability | Quarterly partnership review | ESG Score Contribution | 5% | | **Regulators / Watchdogs** | Compliance, penalties | Continuous monitoring | Legal Incident Count | 5% | | **Investors / Board** | Share‑price, ESG ratings | Quarterly ESG Report | Shareholder Sentiment | 5% | | **Media/Influencers** | Story angle, credibility | Crisis & post‑crisis media briefings | Media Sentiment | 0% | | **Competitive Analysis** | Market share | Monthly competitive scan | Market Share Drop | 0% | *Weighting informs the “Risk‑Adjusted Impact Score” (see §11).* --- ## 5. Tone & Voice Consistency Framework | Tone Category | Rating (1–5) | Narrative Guideline | Approved Phrases | |---------------|--------------|---------------------|-----------------| | **Neutral** | 1 | Fact‑only, no speculation. | “We are monitoring the situation.” | | **Supportive (Non‑Political)** | 2 | Empathic, emphasize service. | “We continue to serve our community with care.” | | **Clarifying** | 3 | Explain brand policy, avoid endorsements. | “Our brand remains committed to safe delivery.” | | **Reassuring** | 4 | Reassure stakeholders of continuity. | “Your trusted supply chain remains uninterrupted.” | | **Defensive** | 5 | Avoid; not permissible for political stance. | – | **Tone‑Scoring Rubric (per document)** - 0–1 % of words → **Neutral** - 1–10 % of emotional language → **Supportive** - 10–25 % → **Clarifying** - 25–40 % → **Reassuring** - > 40 % → **Defensive** (flagged) All RRT drafts are automatically scanned; any > 25 % emotional content triggers a tone‑audit ticket. --- ## 6. Legal & Ethical Compliance Matrix (Country‑Specific) | Country | Law / Guideline | Do | Don’t | Example | |---------|----------------|----|-------|---------| | **France** | *Laïcité* (separation of church & state) | Highlight community partnership, no political color | Endorse political party or candidate | Don’t use the French flag with a political flag | | **Mexico** | *Ley de Defensa del Consumidor* (Consumer Protection) | State product availability, transparency | Disclose political affiliations of brand leaders | Don’t use political slogans on packaging | | **Brazil** | *Marco Regulatório de Combustíveis* (Fuel regulation) | State sustainability credentials, carbon footprint | Political fundraising on social media | Don’t reference political campaign slogans | | **India** | *Election Code of Conduct* | Keep political posts neutral | Any content that may influence voters | Don’t mention election dates | | **South Africa** | *Promotion of Equality Act* | Use inclusive language | Segregative marketing | Don’t use racially charged imagery | *Regulation updates are pulled automatically from local legal feeds into the compliance portal.* --- ## 7. Governance Decision & Timing Flowchart ``` Trigger → LCA Review (≤ 2 h) | v SSC Decision (≤ 24 h) | v RRT Draft (≤ 12 h) | v CCL Release & Monitor (≤ 1 h) | v Post‑Crisis Review (≤ 72 h) ``` *If any node exceeds its time limit, an automatic escalation ticket is created and the Board Executive Committee is notified.* --- ## 8. Post‑Crisis Impact Review Worksheet (Excel template) | Metric | Baseline | Target | Actual (±%) | Action | |--------|----------|--------|------------|--------| | **Sales (units)** | 120 k | 100 k | -15 % | Launch discount drive | | **Revenue** | $4.8 M | $4.5 M | -6 % | Evaluate supply cost | | **NPS** | 65 | 70 | +5 | Enhance CSAT survey | | **CSAT** | 85 % | 90 % | -3 % | Customer support training | | **Share‑of‑Voice** | 3 % | 4 % | +0.5 % | Increase paid media | | **ESG Rating** | B‑ | B+ | N/A | Publish community impact | | **Legal Incidents** | 0 | 0 | 0 | | *The worksheet is auto‑populated from sales, CRM, and sentiment APIs.* --- ## 9. Employee & Franchisee Support Cadence | Channel | Cadence | Content | Owner | KPIs | |---------|---------|---------|-------|------| | Email | **24 h post‑incident** | Executive briefing, FAQ link | EAS | Open Rate 80 % | | Intranet Post | **48 h** | Deep‑dive policy update | EAS | Page Views 60 % | | Town‑Hall Video | **1 wk** | Live Q&A, CEO statement | EAS | Attendance 75 % | | **Franchisee Portal** | **Ongoing** | Real‑time FAQ, Crisis guide | FST | Portal Traffic 90 % | | **Franchisee Pulse Calls** | **Bi‑weekly** | Check‑in, feedback | FST | Call Completion 95 % | | **Employee Slack Bot** | **Daily** | Quick policy reminders | EAS | Interaction Rate 30 % | All communications pass through the tone‑scoring engine and the consistency checker before publishing. --- ## 10. Crisis Timeline: Templated Gantt (Color‑Coded) | Time | Event | Global | Mexico | France | Brazil | |------|-------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | 0‑0:30 h | Trigger | | | | | | 0:30‑1 h | Legal Review | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | | 1‑2 h | SSC Decision | ✔︎ | - | - | - | | 2‑3 h | RRT Draft | | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | | 3‑4 h | CCL Release | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | | 4‑24 h | Monitor & Adjust | | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | | 1‑3 d | Post‑Crisis Review | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | *Gantt displayed in Power BI; teams logged in their local time zones (GMT‑6, GMT‑5, GMT‑1, GMT‑3).* --- ## 11. Tone‑Scoring Rubric (Detailed) | Text Sample | Tone % Scores | Verdict | |-------------|--------------|---------| | “We remain available in all markets, and we’re proud of our community impact.” | 12% emotional | *Clarifying* (4) | | “We’re upset about the allegations, but we’re still proud of our brand.” | 30% emotional | *Defensive* (5 → flag) | | “We’re monitoring the situation and will keep you updated.” | 5% emotional | *Neutral* (1) | The scoring algorithm uses NLP library `textstat` and the custom tone dictionary. --- ## 12. Practical Templates ### 12.1 Global Press Release Template ``` [Company Logo] **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** [Date] **Subject Line:** [Brand] Commits to [Core Value] Amidst Current Events [City, Country] – [CEO Name], CEO of [Brand], today reaffirmed the company’s commitment to [Core Value] and outlined steps to ensure continuity for consumers globally. > “We are actively monitoring developments and remain steadfast in our commitment to delivering quality, safe products to our customers,” said [CEO]. **Key Actions:** - Global supply chain unaffected. - No changes to product pricing or availability. - Continued partnership with local NGOs supporting [relevant cause]. **Legal Disclaimer:** All statements are consistent with local laws and regulations. **Media Contact:** [Name] – Head of Corporate Communications [Phone] | [Email] | [Website] - END – ``` `Placeholders` to be filled by CCL; GPS quote inserted in the quote block; legal disclaimer appended by LCA. ### 12.2 Social Media Carousel (Dual‑Language) | Slide | Image | Spanish Caption | English Caption | Hashtags | |-------|-------|-----------------|-----------------|----------| | 1 | Brand logo | “En todas las comunidades, contamos con un compromiso sólido.” | “In every community, we uphold a solid commitment.” | `#PrincipleStatement #GlobalIntegrity` | | 2 | Recipe shot | “Sabor sin controversia, ¡siempre seguro y auténtico!” | “Flavor without controversy, always safe and authentic!” | `#SafeTaste #ConsumerTrust` | | 3 | Community photo | “Apoyamos a agricultores locales, sin apoyo político.” | “We support local farmers, no political endorsement.” | `#LocalImpact #NoPolitics` | Use `@BrandOfficial` handle and adapt to platform specs. ### 12.3 Internal Memo Style Guide | Element | Standard | Allowed Variation | |---------|----------|-------------------| | **Subject** | “Immediate: Crisis Update – [Topic]” | None | | **Intro** | 4‑line paragraph, factual| None | | **Body** | 2‑bullet points, tone “Clarifying” | | | **Closing** | 1‑line acknowledgement | | | **Length** | ≤ 200 words | | | **Distribution** | All employees, all regions | | All memos auto‑send via internal portal; a copy is archived in the document repository. ### 12.4 Franchisee Support Kit (PDF) - **Front Cover**: “Franchisee Crisis Response Kit – [Brand]” - **Table of Contents** - **Section 1**: Quick FAQ (pre‑approved talking points) - **Section 2**: Customer Script for Phone/Email - **Section 3**: Legal Disclaimer Copy - **Section 4**: Contact List (Crisis Support Hotline, Regional Ops) PDF is distributed via the Franchisee Portal and can be printed by each franchisee. --- ## 13. Lessons‑Learned Heat‑Map | Category | What Worked | What Fell Short | Recommendation | |----------|------------|-----------------|----------------| | **Speed of Response** | RRT drafted within 8 h, surpassing 12 h target | SSC approval delayed 18 h in Region X | Build a “Rapid‑SSC” sub‑committee for high‑impact cases | | **Tone Consistency** | 100 % of posts scored ≤ 3 on tone rubric | 1 post exceeded 25 % emotional language | Enforce mandatory tone‑scan prior to lock‑in | | **Suppliers** | Immediate supply‑chain audit avoided disruption | Supplier‑sourced ingredients flagged for compliance | Expand pre‑audit schedule quarterly | | **Franchisee Support** | FST push of portal resource increased engagement | Franchisees still mis‑communicating on social ads | Add a mandatory 30 min training webinar | | **Employee Morale** | Town‑hall Q&A increased NPS by 4 pts | Some employees still uncertain about policy | Deploy an anonymous pulse survey immediately after crisis | | **ESG Impact** | ESG report updated within 10 days | No mention of crisis effect on rating | Incorporate ESG impact section in reporting | Update the heat‑map after every post‑crisis review; feed into the risk matrix to improve thresholds. --- ## 14. Risk Matrix Quantification | Risk | Impact (1–5) | Likelihood (1–5) | Exposure (Impact × Likelihood) | Mitigation Level | |-----|--------------|------------------|------------------------------|-----------------| | **Legal Penalties** | 5 | 4 | 20 | Immediate escalation to legal | | **Brand Reputation Drop** | 4 | 5 | 20 | 24 h response | | **Supply Chain Disruption** | 3 | 3 | 9 | Supplier pre‑audit | | **Employee Attrition** | 2 | 4 | 8 | Internal support | | **Franchise Dissolution** | 3 | 2 | 6 | Franchisee support | | **Sales Loss** | 4 | 3 | 12 | Targeted promos | | **Social Media Backlash** | 3 | 4 | 12 | Consistency checker | Calculate total exposure; if > 30, the crisis moves to “Level 4” (Board oversight). --- ## 15. Cross‑Channel Consistency Checker (Technical Solution) - **Tool:** `consistency-checker.py` (Python 3.10) - **Inputs:** All public documents (press, social, internal) + global GPS. - **Outputs:** JSON report: mismaches ≤ 50 characters flagged. - **Automation:** Ran every 15 min via Azure Function; alerts sent to Slack #crisis‑check group. - **Threshold:** Any “Tone‑Defensive” > 25 % or “Dos & Don’ts” violation triggers an automatic block until resolved. --- ## 16.
